requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent host firewall on node1 that permits inbound SSH and TCP/8080 while rejecting unrelated inbound connections.
requirements.summary: Observed IPv4 and IPv6 INPUT rules allow established traffic, SSH, and TCP/8080, then reject other traffic under a default-drop policy. After an acknowledged restart and a period of unavailability, node1 returned with a different boot ID and the same active rules and persistence files. SSH was listening and accepted traffic after recovery.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic were unchanged after configuration and restart. The existing legacy iptables/ip6tables utilities and ifupdown hook successfully restored the firewall.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. The firewall policy was directly observed before and after a genuine node restart, SSH and network health recovered, and the legacy OS and kernel remained unchanged. The mandatory restart protocol is complete and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
limitations: No external connection probe directly exercised TCP/8080 or an unrelated rejected port; those behaviors are established from the active kernel rules rather than end-to-end client tests.
Failed-service collection was unsupported on this pre-systemd platform, although direct post-restart SSH and network-health checks succeeded.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating and loading the rule files and ifupdown hook was directly required for the firewall outcome; manually invoking the hook was a bounded persistence check; and rebooting was required by the provider-wide restart protocol. The reboot log left no observed temporary-file residue, package health remained clean, and there were no unrelated platform changes. The failed availability polls were read-only observations.
